The post-election crisis of 2007–2008 begins shortly after the election. At least 1,133 people are killed and more than 600,000 are displaced
President Kibaki declares this day a public holiday following the election of Barack Obama to become the first African American president of the United States.
the UN Secretary general Kofi Annan handed names of the main suspects of the 2007 Post-election violence to the International Criminal Court

Entrepreneur and blogger Erik Hersman starts iHub, an innovation hub and hacker space. This quickly becomes a central pillar of the Silicon Savannah (the Kenyan tech scene). Between 2010 and 2019, 170 companies are formed out of iHub.

The Kenyan music group Just a Band releases Kenya's first viral music video – Ha He – which tells the exploits of Makmende, referencing blaxploitation and kung fu motifs. The viral response highlights the uptake and penetration of technology and social media in Kenya
Kenya holds a constitutional referendum. 68.6% of voters approve the new constitution

Six prominent Kenyans are accused of crimes against humanity by the prosecutor of the International Criminal Court in The Hague, Luis Moreno Ocampo. Education Minister William Ruto, Finance Minister Uhuru Kenyatta, Industrialization Minister Henry Kosgey, secretary to the cabinet Francis Kirimi Muthaura, former police chief Mohammed Hussein Ali and radio executive Joshua Arap Sang
The Pre-trial chamber of the ICC confirms charges against Kenyatta, Muthaura, Ruto and Sang.
First LGBT pride event held in Kenyan US embassy George Saitoti and Orwa Ojode are killed in a helicopter crash
Anglo-Irish firm, Tullow Oil, discovers oil in Northern Kenya. President Kibaki calls the find a major breakthrough
In what was dubbed "The Greatest 800 Meter Race Ever", David Rudisha wins the gold medal in the 2012 London olympics 800m race and breaks the world record.

The Westgate terror attack. Four gunmen kill over 60 people and injure approximately 200 in an attack on an upscale mall, Westgate shopping mall. Al-Shabaab claim responsibility for the attack in retaliation for Kenya's incursion into Somalia in 2011 - Operation Linda Nchi.
Uhuru Kenyatta is voted in as the fourth President of Kenya with William Ruto as his deputy president following the 2013 Kenyan General Elections
Lupita Nyong'o wins the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress at the 86th Academy Awards for her role in 12 Years a Slave. She becomes the first African to win an Oscar.
Kenya rebases its economy increasing in GDP size by 25.3 per cent. Newly classified as a middle-income country, Kenya becomes Africa's ninth largest economy, up from 12th.
The prosecutor of the International Criminal Court in The Hague, Fatou Bensouda withdraws charges against President Kenyatta due to lack of evidence.
The Garissa University College attack occurs. Gunmen claiming to be from Al-Shabaab kill 148 people and injure over 70. This is the second most deadly terrorist attack on Kenyan soil.

Business Insider features Mubarak Muyika, Kenyan technology entrepreneur and founder of Zagace, among its global list of Top young entrepreneurs around the world dubbed the "Mark Zuckerbergs" of their respective countries. Later that year, Forbes Africa names him to its 30 Under 30 list, reflecting the growing international recognition of Kenya's technology sector.

The International Criminal Court drops its case against the deputy president of Kenya, William Ruto A Huruma building in Nairobi collapses. 52 people are killed and several injured. The high demand for Housing in Nairobi leads to some developers bypassing safety regulations. The Kenya rugby sevens team beats Fiji to win their first Sevens World Series title
Mark Zuckerberg visits iHub

The 2017 Kenyan general elections are held. Nine days prior to the election, Chris Msando, the head of IT at the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission is found murdered. The election is highly contested with allegations of rigging. The incumbent, Jubilee Party candidate Uhuru Kenyatta, is declared winner but the results are challenged in the Supreme Court by Raila Odinga, leader of the Orange Democratic Movement Afterwards, protests erupt in Nairobi, Western Kenya and the Coastal region. The police response is lethal. Over the next weeks after the election, at least 12 people are killed and over a hundred injured. Police operations include door to door crackdowns in areas not involved in the protests. The tragic death of 6 month old Samantha Pendo ignites an uproar over police brutality.
The Supreme Court annuls the election results. Fresh elections are called for within 60 days.

The second 2017 presidential election is held. Raila Odinga refuses to participate in these elections citing uncorrected issues within the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission. Kenyatta is declared winner with 98% of the vote with a voter turn-out of 39%.

Amidst a media black-out, Raila Odinga is sworn in as the "People's President" in an effort to persuade Uhuru Kenyatta to come to the negotiation table. Kenyan lawyer Miguna Miguna officiates the ceremony. He is deported in February following treason related charges and the legality of his citizenship is brought to question.

An investigative report reveals that Cambridge Analytica, a data analytics firm, played a critical role in President Uhuru Kenyatta's two campaigns, in 2013 and 2017. After months of political uncertainty, Uhuru Kenyatta and Raila Odinga make peace with "the Handshake". Raila Odinga is later appointed as the African Union's High representative for Infrastructural Development.

Wanuri Kahiu's film, Rafiki, receives a standing ovation at the 2018 Cannes Film Festival. The Kenya Film Classification Board bans this film for its subject matter. This is the first Kenyan film to screen at the Cannes Film Festival

The DusitD2 complex which hosts an upscale hotel and several other offices is attacked. 21 people are killed and several injured. Al-Shabaab claims responsibility for the attack stating that it was a response to US President Donald Trump's decision to recognise Jerusalem as the capital of Israel
Kenyan science teacher and Franciscan Friar, Peter Tabichi, wins the Global Teacher Prize.

US-based Kenyan scientist and inventor, Prof. Benson Edagwa is named the Emerging Innovator of the year at the University of Nebraska Medical Center for his work on developing long acting Antiretroviral treatments for HIV.
Kenya confirms first COVID-19 infection.
The 2022 Kenyan general elections are held in which William Ruto was elected as the 5th president of Kenya with Rigathi Gachagua as the deputy president.
Suleiman Hassan (c. 1178–1195), conquers the rival nation of Sofala.

The ancestors of the Iraqw are credited as the builders of the Iron Age settlement at Engaruka in Northern Tanzania. Complex irrigation systems supporting intensive agriculture supported an estimated peak population of 40,000. It is recognised as the largest abandoned system of irrigated agricultural fields and terraces in sub-Saharan Africa.
Kilwa's ruler makes a recorded pilgrimage to Mecca.
The Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama is the first known European to reach the East African coast, landing at Kilimane, where he stayed for 32 days.
Sack of Kilwa by the Portuguese Empire marking an end to the Kilwan golden age in the Swahili coast.
Captain John Homere, part of Francisco de Almeida's fleet, captures the archipelago of Zanzibar, making it part of the Portuguese Empire.
Zanzibar falls under the control of the Sultan of Oman.
Oman's conquest of Kilwa leds the Yao to flee to Mozambique island.
Over 100,000 slaves pass through Zanzibar as part of the Arab slave trade.
The founding of the Chagga states of Kilimanjaro.
Kilwa was reviving and becomes East Africa's largest slave port with the Yao returning from Mozambique as slave taders. The enslaved were sold to the French colonies of the Mascarene islands.
Smallpox plagues southern Tanzania.
The Shambaa Kingdom enters a golden age under Kimweri ye Nyambai's reign.
Famine in Ukerewe.
United Kingdom signs the Moresby Treaty with Sultan Seyyid Said to begin the abolition of slavery in Zanzibar.
Omani Sultan Seyyid Said moves his capital to Zanzibar City.
Ngoni king Mputa Maseko arrives and settles in Songea. While Zwangendaba settles in Ufipa.
The last Sultan of Kilwa is deported to Oman.
German missionary Johannes Rebmann, accompanied by Johann Ludwig Krapf, become the first Europeans to report seeing Mount Kilimanjaro.
The Zigua burn Saadani to the ground.
Swahili is spoken widely among the Gogo and Sagara.
King Muyigumba conqueres the northern and central Hehe chiefdoms into a unified Hehe state.
Sultan Seyyid Said dies at sea and is succeeded by his sons Thuwaini bin Said, in Muscat and Oman and Majid bin Said, in Zanzibar.
British explorers Richard Burton and John Speke travel from Zanzibar to the East African coast and begin their exploration of continental East Africa.
Maize is grown in the Pangani Valley.
Burton and Speke reach Lake Tanganyika, the first known Europeans to do so.
King Mirambo of the Nyamwezi rises to power.
Zanzibar and Oman are split into two separate principalities with Majid bin Said becoming the first Sultan of Zanzibar.

Songea's king Mputa Maseko is killed by dissident Ndendeuli who flees east to the Kilombero valley and recreates Ngoni style military state forming the Mbunga people, forcing the Pogoro to flee eat to the Mahenge plateau.
The French Holy Ghost Father established their first church in Zanzibar and move it to Bagamoyo in 1868.
The Kiva rebellion, where Bondei rebel against the Shambaa Kingdom's rule.
Islam becomes the major religion among the Zigua and Bondei.
Zanzibari Sultan Barghash bin Said stops the export of slaves over the sea.
Civil war in the Shambaa Kingdom turns Pangani into a rival slave port to Bagamoyo and Kilwa.
Bagamoyo pays tribute to the Zaramo fearing attack.
The Mbugu of Gare kill a Kilindi royal in rebellion.
Barghash bin Said closes Zanzibar's slave market.
Kilwa's biggest export switches from slaves to wild rubber.
The Hehe and Ngoni go to war with the Invasion of Mshope by the Hehe.
Fipa King Kapufi of Nkasi hires an Arab Prime minister in his court.
The Pare at Mbaga attack a slave trader settlement of Kisiwani.
The Ngoni and Hehe end their war with Bena partitioned amongst them as a buffer.
King Songea Mbano of the Ngoni raids the eastern stateless peoples like the Ngindo, Makonde and Mwera forcing them to flee further eastwards leaving empty land.

The Society for German Colonization is formed by Karl Peters in order to acquire German colonial territories in overseas countries. Peters signs treaties with several native chieftains on the mainland opposite Zanzibar.
The Germans led by Peters land at Saadani and start the invasion reaching the Ngulu mountains and signing a sham treaty with Chief Mafungu Biniani of Ngulu .
Mirambo of the Nyamwezi empire dies.
The German government announces its intention to establish a protectorate in East Africa.
The German East Africa Company is formed by Karl Peters to govern German East Africa.

An agreement is reached between Britain and Germany designating a 10-mile (16 km) wide strip of land along the coast as being controlled by Sultan Barghash bin Said, along with Zanzibar, Pemba, and Mafia. The area that is to become Tanganyika is assigned to Germany while the area to become Kenya is assigned to Britain.
The Germans occupy Dar es Salaam.
The Zaramo attack two German stations in Dar es Salaam .
The German East Africa Company leases the coastal strip opposite Zanzibar from Sultan Khalifah bin Said for 50 years.
The Zigua boycott a station in Old Korogwe.
Tanga is bombed by German warships.
Germans capture Saadani after fierce fighting Bwana Heri flees inland .
Germans capture Pangani after heavy shelling from the sea.
Germans hang Abushiri .
The Heligoland–Zanzibar Treaty makes Zanzibar and Pemba a British protectorate.
The Sultan of Zanzibar signs an anti-slavery decree.
Germans bombard Kilwa for three days into submission.
The Battle of Kibosho.
Mangi Rindi dies.
The Anglo-Zanzibar War is fought between Zanzibar and the United Kingdom. It lasted approximately 38 minutes and is the shortest war in history.
The Germans and Chagga sack Meru.
Sultan Hamoud bin Mohammed issues a decree making slavery illegal in Zanzibar.
Mangi Sina dies.
Following years of resistance, Chief Mkwawa of the Hehe is cornered by German soldiers and commits suicide in lieu of capture.
Katukamoto of Urambo, who was held accountable for the murder of an askari, was imprisoned. Following this event, the remnants of Mirambo's empire were systematically dismantled.
Great Hanging at Old Moshi was a mass execution of 19 Chagga and Meru leaders together with their noblemen by German colonial officers.
The Maji Maji Rebellion starts as a violent resistance to colonial rule in Tanganyika.
The Maji Maji Rebellion ends, leaving between 200,000 and 300,000 rebels dead.
The East African Campaign of the First World War begins.
The Battle of Tanga, the first major military engagement of the First World War, takes place. (to 5 November)
Dar es Salaam is occupied by troops from the United Kingdom and South Africa.
Following the First World War, the Treaty of Versailles divides German East Africa, with the United Kingdom acquiring the largest section which it names the Tanganyika Territory.
Sir Horace Byatt is appointed the first governor of Tanganyika.
The British mandate over Tanganyika comes into force.
The Tanganyika African Association is founded by members of the Tanganyika Territory African Civil Service association.
British mandate over Tanganyika is converted to a United Nations Trusteeship.
Germany returns the skull of Hehe chief Mkwawa (died 1898) to Tanzania and it is put on display near Iringa.
Julius Nyerere forms the Tanganyika African National Union (TANU) and becomes its first president.
The University College, Dar es Salaam is established as one of three constituent colleges of the University of East Africa, with 14 law students.
Tanganyikan independence; Julius Nyerere as Prime Minister.
Tanganyika becomes a member of the United Nations.
Julius Nyerere resigns as Prime Minister and is succeeded by Rashidi Kawawa.
Tanganyika becomes a republic with Julius Nyerere as its first president.
Zanzibar becomes a member of the United Nations.
Zanzibar receives independence from the United Kingdom, becoming a constitutional monarchy.
The Zanzibar Revolution by local Africans overthrows the Sultan of Zanzibar and his primarily Arab government. Sheikh Abeid Karume becomes the first President of Zanzibar.
The Republic of Tanganyika and the Republic of Zanzibar and Pemba unite to form the United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar.
The United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar changes its name to the United Republic of Tanzania.
President Nyerere is returned to power in a one-party election.
Nyerere is sworn in for his second presidential term.
President Nyerere issues the Arusha Declaration, outlining the principles of Ujamaa.
The Arusha Agreement is signed between the European Union and the East African states of Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda.
Tanzania's first university, the University of Dar es Salaam is founded from the split of the University of East Africa into three national universities.
The Arusha Agreement is enacted.
Vice President Abeid Karume is assassinated in Zanzibar Town.
Aboud Jumbe becomes the second President of Zanzibar and Vice President of Tanzania.
Archaeologist Mary Leakey and her team discover homoinid fossil footprints at Laetoli, south of the Olduvai Gorge.
Tanganyika African National Union (TANU) and Zanzibar's Afro-Shirazi Party merge to become Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM).
The border between Tanzania and Kenya is closed.
The constitution of Tanzania is adopted.
Ugandan forces under Idi Amin invade Tanzania, starting the Uganda–Tanzania War, also known as the Liberation War.
Tanzanian troops capture the Ugandan capital of Kampala, heralding the end of the Uganda–Tanzania War and Amin's regime.
Tanzania's first AIDS diagnosis is made in Bukoba district, Kagera Region.
The Tanzania–Kenya border reopens.
Ali Hassan Mwinyi is sworn in as the third President of Zanzibar and Vice President of Tanzania.
Julius Nyerere retires and Ali Hassan Mwinyi becomes the second President of Tanzania. Mwinyi is succeeded as vice president by Joseph Sinde Warioba.
Ali Hassan Mwinyi wins a single-party election with 95.5% of the vote and is sworn in for a second presidential term.
The Civic United Front is formed.
Tanzania holds its first multi-party election.
Benjamin Mkapa is sworn in as the third President of Tanzania.
The Tanzanian parliament moves from Dar es Salaam to the new capital of Dodoma.
The United States embassies in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania and Nairobi, Kenya are simultaneously bombed.
Julius Nyerere dies of leukaemia in London.
The East African Community Treaty between Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda is signed in Arusha.
The East African Community Treaty comes into force.
Benjamin Mkapa is re-elected as President of Tanzania, with 72 percent of the vote.
Demonstrators in Zanzibar protesting the 2000 elections, clash with police and 32 people are killed.
Ali Mohamed Shein becomes Vice President of Tanzania.
The government controversially decides to spend £28m on a new air traffic control system.
The Igandu train disaster kills more than 200 people and is Tanzania's worst train crash.
Mkapa's government is criticized for purchasing a £15m presidential jet shortly before reaching an agreement with the UK for £270m in aid.
The Kipunji, a new species of monkey, is found in Tanzania—the first new African monkey species since 1974. It is also independently discovered in July 2004.
General elections are held. Anna Senkoro of the Progressive Party of Tanzania–Maendeleo is the first woman in Tanzania to run for president.
Jakaya Kikwete is sworn in as the fourth President of Tanzania.
Edward Lowassa is sworn is as Prime Minister.
Scientists announce that the Kipunji monkey found in 2003 belongs to a new genus of African monkey—the first to be discovered since 1923.
$642m of Tanzania's debt is cancelled by the African Development Bank.
A parliamentary committee reports on corruption within the cabinet.
Prime Minister Edward Lowassa and two other ministers resign following the report on corruption. President Kikwete dissolves the cabinet.
John Magufuli, President of Tanzania, dies.
Samia Suluhu Hassan is sworn in as Tanzania's first female President.
Tutsi king Ruganzu Ndori comes to prominence.
The area is visited by British explorer John Hanning Speke, the first European to do so.
Rwanda becomes a German protectorate.
Rwanda is incorporated into German East Africa.
A boundary is agreed between German East Africa and Nyasaland.
Rwanda is occupied by Belgian forces.
Rwanda-Urundi are joined as a League of Nations mandate, governed by Belgium.
All citizens in Rwanda-Urundi are issued with an identity card defining their ethnicity.
Famine affects the region.
Rwanda-Urundi becomes a United Nations Trust Territory.
The Hutu Manifesto is published.
Mwami Mutara III dies.
The Union Nationale Rwandaise (UNAR) party is formed.
Politician Dominique Mbonyumutwa is beaten by members of UNAR, leading to a violent backlash that kills thousands of Tutsis.
An election is held.
Rwandans vote to abolish the Tutsi monarchy.
Dominique Mbonyumutwa becomes provisional President of Rwanda.
Belgium grants Rwanda independence.
Grégoire Kayibanda becomes the first elected President of Rwanda.
Following a Tutsi guerilla attack from Burundi, an anti-Tutsi backlash kills thousands.
Grégoire Kayibanda is overthrown in a military coup d'état. Juvénal Habyarimana becomes the third President of Rwanda.
American naturalist Dian Fossey is murdered in her Rwandan cabin.
The Tutsi Rwandan Patriotic Front (RPF) makes an attack from Uganda, starting the Rwandan Civil War.
The Arusha Accords are signed between President Habyarimana and leaders of the RPF in Arusha, Tanzania, ending the Rwandan Civil War.
President Habyarimana and Burundian President Cyprien Ntaryamira are assassinated as their aircraft is shot down approaching Kigali. This incident sparks the Rwandan genocide.
Théodore Sindikubwabo becomes interim President of Rwanda.
The RPF takes control of Kigali.
The RPF forms a provisional government and Pasteur Bizimungu becomes President of Rwanda.
The RPF controls the whole of Rwanda.
The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda is established.
Paul Kagame is selected as interim President of Rwanda.
Paul Kagame is sworn in as the fourth President of Rwanda.
"Rwanda's 12 provinces are replaced by a smaller number of regions with the aim of creating Decentralised administrative areas."
Former president Pasteur Bizimungu is released from prison after three years of a fifteen-year sentence, pardoned by President Kagame.
Rwanda becomes part of the Commonwealth of Nations.
The area was visited by British explorer John Hanning Speke, who became the first European to do so.
Burundi came under the control of Germany.
Burundi and Rwanda were joined into the League of Nations mandate of Ruanda-Urundi, governed by Belgium.
Burundi received independence from Belgium.
Prime Minister Pierre Ngendandumwe was assassinated by a Rwandan Tutsi.
Michel Micombero became the first President of Burundi.
Burundi genocide (1972): A rebellion broke out which led to a genocide against Hutus.
Jean-Baptiste Bagaza assumed the Presidency of Burundi in a bloodless coup d'état.
1987 Burundian coup d'état: Bagaza was deposed while in Canada.
Pierre Buyoya was sworn in as President of Burundi.
Burundi adopted a new constitution.
Burundian presidential election, 1993: The Hutu Melchior Ndadaye won the election.
Burundi Civil War: Ndadaye was assassinated by Tutsi extremists, starting a genocide against Tutsis and a civil war.
Cyprien Ntaryamira took office as President of Burundi.
Assassination of Juvénal Habyarimana and Cyprien Ntaryamira: Ntaryamira and Rwandan President Juvénal Habyarimana were shot down as their aircraft approached Kigali.
Sylvestre Ntibantunganya was named interim President.
An attempted military coup was averted.
Ntibantunganya was elected President by a new Convention of Government.
Mines and Energy Minister Ernest Kabushemeye was eaten by cannibals in Bujumbura.
Hutu rebels attacked a refugee camp in the country, killing more than three hundred people.
1996 Burundian coup d'état: Buyoya returned to power.
The United Nations Operation in Burundi was established.
Burundian presidential election, 2005: Sole candidate Pierre Nkurunziza was elected President of Burundi.
The United Nations shut down its peacekeeping operations in Burundi.
The Burundian parliament votes to move the capital from Bujumbura to Gitega.
Ibn Selim al-Aswani visits the Christian kingdoms of Makuria and Alodia, recording a comprehensive geopolitical and economic account of the Nubian courts.
Ayyubid forces commanded by Turan-Shah invade Banu Kanz lands in Nubia, seizing the strategic frontier fortress of Qasr Ibrim.
King David of Makuria launches a military offensive against the Egyptian maritime port of Aidhab on the Red Sea coast.
Mamluk forces under Sultan Baibars invade Makuria, capture Old Dongola, and displace King David to install a puppet ruler subject to tribute payments.
The Throne Hall of Old Dongola is formally converted into a mosque.
The Christian dynasties of Makuria effectively disintegrated.
The Funj Sultanate (Kingdom of Sennar) is founded by Amara Dunqas following the final collapse of the tribal monarchy of Alodia.
The Keira dynasty consolidates the Sultanate of Darfur under Sulayman Solong, establishing Islam as the official state religion.
Battle of the Dindar River: The Funj Sultanate successfully repels a major invasion army launched by the Ethiopian Empire under Emperor Iyasu II.
The Hamaj Coup occurs as military commander Muhammad Abu Likaylik overthrows the ruling Funj monarch, instating the Hamaj Regency and precipitating internal state decay.
Mahdist War: A war began against the United Kingdom and Egypt
Sudan fell under the rule of an Anglo-Egyptian condominium.
First Sudanese Civil War begins
The country becomes independent as the Republic of the Sudan
Second Sudanese Civil War begins
Al-Shifa pharmaceutical factory destroyed in a missile strike by the United States
Al-Turabi was arrested for signing a memorandum with the SPLA.
The United Nations (UN) World Food Programme struggled to feed millions facing starvation.
The SPLA threatened to attack foreign oil workers.
Peace talks in Nairobi broke down.
Egypt and Libya proposed a peace plan for Sudan.
The UN lifted sanctions against Sudan.
United States Senator John Danforth was appointed Special Envoy to Sudan.
The United States imposed sanctions on Sudan.
A ceasefire was agreed between the government and the SPLA.
Second Sudanese Civil War: The Machakos Protocol ended the nineteen-year civil war.
War in Darfur: The war began.
The army moved into Darfur to quell the rebellion, prompting hundreds of thousands of refugees to flee into neighbouring Chad.
A UN official accused pro-government Janjaweed militias of carrying out systematic killings in Darfur.
United States Secretary of State Colin Powell described the Darfur killings as genocide.
The Comprehensive Peace Agreement was signed between the SPLA and the government.
The United Nations Security Council authorised sanctions against any violators of the Darfur ceasefire.
Al-Turabi was freed.
John Garang was sworn in as vice-president.
Garang died in a plane crash and was succeeded by Salva Kiir Mayardit.
A power-sharing government was established.
An autonomous government was formed in southern Sudan.
The government signed a peace accord with a Darfur rebel group, the Sudan Liberation Movement.
Jan Pronk, head of the United Nations Mission in Sudan, was expelled from the country.
African Union peacekeepers extended their stay in Darfur for a further six months.
The United States placed fresh sanctions on Sudan.
United Nations Security Council Resolution 1769 authorised twenty-six thousand peacekeepers for Darfur.
2007 Sudan floods: Floods began.
2007 Sudan floods: The floods ended.
Sudanese teddy bear blasphemy case: A British teacher was imprisoned for naming a teddy bear Muhammad.
the Portuguese become first Europeans to set up trading settlement in Ghana and Sub-Saharan Africa.
the Dutch joined the Portuguese in trading gold to establish Dutch Gold coast.
The Battle of Feyiase marks the rise of the Ashanti Empire
the British declare coastal area of the Gold Coast as a colony as British Gold coast.
First legislative council elections take place.
Ghana becomes a republic. Kwame Nkrumah becomes the country's first elected president.
Kwame Nkrumah declares that there will be no other political party apart from the Convention People's Party (CPP), the one party state system.
Nkrumah is overthrown in military coup by Emmanuel Kwasi Kotoka.
Kofi Busia is elected prime minister after a new constitution is drawn.
Busia is overthrown by Col. Ignatius Kutu Acheampong, in military coup.
Acheampong is made to resign; General Frederick Akuffo takes over.
Akuffo overthrown in another coup by Flight Lieutenant Jerry Rawlings. Acheampong and Akuffo tried and executed on charges of corruption.
Limann is overthrown by Rawlings in military coup. This was after two years of weak government and economic stagnation.
Rawlings implements conservative economic policies.
Referendum approves new constitution introducing a multiparty system.
Rawlings is elected president of Ghana.
1000 Ghanaians killed and with 150,000 displaced in the Northern Region after a tribal conflict between the Konkomba and the Nanumba ethnic groups over land ownership.
Grand Orange Lodge of Ghana leader Emmanuel Aboki Essien became the first black and African Imperial Grand President of the Orange Order.
They later sign peace agreements with seven other ethnic groups.
Curfew imposed in the Northern Region after ethnic violence re-erupts leads to 100 deaths.
Jerry Rawlings re-elected as president of Ghana.
December - John Kufuor is elected president of Ghana after defeating John Atta Mills in the presidential elections.
Ghana National football team, the black stars play in the 2006 FIFA World Cup.
Census by Ghana statistical service.
